project: Lando v4 Compose Service-Key Vocabulary (post-freeze feature wave, 4.1 target)
description: Makes the amended spec sections 6.2, 7.4, and 5.5.1 true: Compose compatibility as a service-key vocabulary, not a file-format promise. US-466..US-467 (PRD-01) build the alignment substrate: the Compose JSON Schema vendored from a tagged compose-spec/compose-go release and pinned by checksum, the committed key-disposition matrix (normalized | preserved | rejected) with the check:compose-coverage gate that fails CI on any unclassified upstream key path, and the automated upstream-bump workflow. US-468..US-472 (PRD-02) land the vocabulary normalizations: Compose spellings and alternate forms (depends_on incl. condition map, working_dir, env_file, list environment, labels), ports/expose and volumes long syntax with mounts/storage/tmpfs classification, the Compose healthcheck shape, build: shape discrimination replacing composeBuild (pre-release gut-and-replace), and depends_on conditions driving section 6.13 orchestration. US-473..US-474 (PRD-03) land the per-container runtime-knob tier: schema shapes for the section 6.2 knob list with lossless preservation into ServicePlan.extensions.compose and the section 5.5.1 capability check with tagged CapabilityError, then Podman realization of the common knobs. US-475..US-482 (PRD-04) land the rejection surface, fixture-driven conformance, the binding native-field prerequisite, parser/tooling follow-ups, and the closeout story: generated docs key matrix, executable guide, and SDK snapshot/API-compatibility reconciliation. Source of truth remains spec/{01..19}-*.md; when PRDs and normative spec disagree, the spec wins and both must be reconciled together. All stories carry full TDD acceptance criteria, plus Tests pass, Typecheck passes, and Lint passes criteria.

userStories.title: Vendored pinned schema, disposition matrix, and coverage gate
userStories.description: As a core maintainer, the upstream Compose JSON Schema is vendored in-repo pinned to a tagged compose-spec/compose-go release with a checksum, every key path in its service subtree carries exactly one committed disposition (normalized | preserved | rejected), and CI fails the moment the schema and the matrix disagree in either direction.
acceptanceCriteria: vendor/compose/compose-spec.json is committed, byte-identical to schema/compose-spec.json at the pinned compose-go tag; vendor/compose/pin.json records { tag, sourceUrl, sha256 } and the vendored file's checksum matches.

`bun run codegen:compose-vendor` fetches the schema for the pinned tag, verifies the checksum, and rewrites the vendored file; it is the only network-touching path and is not invoked by tests or offline codegen gates.
An offline unit test verifies the vendored-file checksum against pin.json so manual edits to the vendored schema fail CI.

A committed matrix module (e.g. core/src/landofile/compose/dispositions.ts) maps every service-subtree key path of the vendored schema to normalized | preserved | rejected, with a rationale per entry and remediation pointers on rejected entries.

`bun run check:compose-coverage` walks the vendored schema (resolving $refs, oneOf short/long forms, patternProperties), and fails listing schema key paths with no matrix entry and matrix entries with no schema key path, following existing check:* gate conventions.
Top-level project keys (services, volumes, networks, configs, secrets, include, version, name, x-*) are covered by a static classification asserted by the same gate.
The gate runs in CI alongside the other boundary gates; the workflow generator is updated and regenerated output is committed together.
The initial matrix classifies the full current vendored schema per spec 6.2/7.4 (normalized set, knob tier preserved, rejected list) with the gate green.
Unit tests cover the schema walker on a fixture schema; root AGENTS.md generated-files note gains the vendored path (generator-owned).
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: Origin: spec 7.4 'Vendored upstream schema' + 'Disposition matrix' rules; spec 5.5.1 (planning consults the matrix). Pin source MUST be a compose-go tag, never the untagged compose-spec mirror. The matrix is the single source for the coverage gate, the published docs matrix (US-477), rejection remediation text (US-475), and the fixture skip-list (US-476). Merged from former US-466 + US-467.

userStories.title: Automated upstream-bump workflow
userStories.description: As a core maintainer, when compose-go publishes a new tagged release, a PR appears that bumps the pin and vendored schema and cannot go green until any new key paths are classified.
acceptanceCriteria: A scheduled generated workflow checks the latest compose-go tag against pin.json and, when newer, runs codegen:compose-vendor with the new tag and opens/updates a single rolling PR with the pin + vendored diff.
The PR body lists added/removed key paths versus the previous vendored schema (US-466 walker reused as a diff reporter).
check:compose-coverage failing on unclassified new keys is the intended merge blocker; the diff reporter is tested against a synthetic schema bump; no auto-classification is attempted.
The workflow is emitted by the workflow generator (never hand-edited), follows nightly-workflow conventions, and `git diff --exit-code` on generated paths is clean after `bun run codegen`.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: Origin: spec 7.4 'bumping the pin is a deliberate act'. Generated workflows are codegen outputs per root AGENTS.md; edit the generator, not the YAML. Blocked by US-466.

acceptanceCriteria: Long-form port entries decode; short strings ('8080:80', '127.0.0.1:8080:80/udp', '80') parse per the Compose port grammar into the same long form; invalid grammar fails with position-carrying remediation.

ports and expose normalize into endpoints; host bindings require the provider host-port capability per spec 6.2; published port ranges ('8000-8010:8000-8010') either normalize or reject per their matrix disposition, never silently dropped.
services.<name>.endpoints continues to win over ports-inferred intent, tested.
Long-form volumes entries decode; short strings ('./src:/app', 'named:/data:ro', '/data') parse into the same long form.

Volume classification per spec 6.2: host-path sources -> mounts, named volumes -> storage, anonymous volumes -> storage auto-naming (spec 6.5), type: tmpfs -> the preserved tmpfs runtime knob (US-473 shape).
read_only, volume.subpath, and bind.create_host_path map to mount-model equivalents; unsupported sub-fields follow their matrix disposition with tests proving no silent drop.

userStories.title: depends_on conditions drive orchestration
userStories.description: As a user, condition: service_healthy and service_completed_successfully actually gate start/build ordering per spec 6.13, not just parse.
acceptanceCriteria: Plan dependency edges carry the condition; service_started remains the default for list-form depends_on and Lando dependsOn.
service_healthy: dependents' start/app-build steps wait on the dependency's healthcheck success; a service_healthy edge onto a dependency with no healthcheck fails planning with remediation.
service_completed_successfully: dependents wait on the dependency's successful exit; non-zero exit fails waiting steps with the spec 6.13 continue-all aggregation.
required: false tolerates an absent/failed optional dependency per Compose semantics; restart: true follows its matrix disposition.
Orchestrator tests cover all three conditions deterministically via the test provider.

userStories.title: Knob-tier shapes, lossless preservation, and capability check
userStories.description: As a user, every spec 6.2 runtime knob (restart, cap_add/cap_drop, privileged, devices, ulimits, sysctls, tmpfs, shm_size, dns*, extra_hosts, init, stop_signal, stop_grace_period, security_opt, group_add, read_only, platform, pull_policy, logging, gpus, deploy.resources) decodes in each form Compose defines and is preserved losslessly into ServicePlan.extensions.compose — and on a provider that cannot realize a knob I used, planning fails up front with a tagged CapabilityError naming the knob, the service, and the provider.

Multi-form keys canonicalize to one long form; byte/duration strings parse with remediation on invalid grammar.
The planner copies canonicalized knobs into ServicePlan.extensions.compose with a round-trip test proving losslessness for every key.
Planning collects the preserved knobs in use per service and checks them against the selected provider's composeSpec capability declaration before any provider action.
Providers declare knob support as part of the composeSpec capability surface; the declaration shape is published in @lando/sdk and covered by the provider contract suite.
An unsupported knob yields a CapabilityError carrying { service, key, provider } plus remediation, rendered through the CLI failure formatter and the machine-output envelope.
The test provider declares a partial knob set so accept and reject paths are both covered deterministically.
Each key's matrix entry is preserved; check:compose-coverage green.

userStories.title: Podman realization of the common knobs
userStories.description: As a user on the bundled Podman provider, the common runtime knobs take real effect in the created container.
acceptanceCriteria: The Podman provider maps to libpod create-container fields: restart, cap_add/cap_drop, privileged, devices, ulimits, sysctls, tmpfs, shm_size, dns/dns_search/dns_opt, extra_hosts, init, stop_signal, stop_grace_period, security_opt, group_add, read_only, platform, and logging.

logging is declared on Linux, macOS, and Windows because Podman consumes its complete driver plus options shape and rejects invalid values loudly; the provider additionally rejects the remote-incompatible passthrough and passthrough-tty drivers before container creation. pull_policy, gpus, and deploy.resources are excluded from the capability declaration on every host platform in this wave because the frozen key-level capability contract cannot honestly represent their supported value or subfield subsets, so the US-473 check rejects them before provider action rather than best-effort or silently partial realization.
The provider's declared knob set exactly matches the implemented mapping, asserted by a declaration-vs-mapping diff test.
Unit tests cover request-body construction per knob; live effects (privileged, ulimit, extra_hosts) verified in the env-gated LANDO_TEST_PODMAN_SOCKET integration suite, serial per repo convention.
Windows named-pipe and Linux socket transports both exercised where CI supports them.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Lint passes

userStories.title: Conformance fixture suite
userStories.description: As a core maintainer, the vocabulary is proven against upstream Compose fixture material on every CI run, and the skip-list cannot quietly hide unsupported-but-classified-supported behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: US-482 is a binding prerequisite for story completion: US-476 MUST remain passes: false until US-482 passes, and once US-482 passes that prerequisite is satisfied. This sequencing rule does not authorize US-476 to implement or reintroduce US-482's production surface. Fixtures expressly assigned to US-482 may share and execute through the US-476 harness without becoming US-476 production scope or broadening US-476's fixture-ownership proof. Service-level fixtures vendored from compose-spec/conformance-tests plus a curated real-world corpus (depends_on-condition, long-form ports/volumes, list-env, Compose-healthcheck patterns) live under core/test/fixtures/compose/. US-476 fixture ownership is limited to normalized and preserved production behavior implemented before US-476; discovering any other missing production contract creates a binding prerequisite story and MUST NOT add that behavior inside the fixture story. Whole-branch accounting MUST attribute production schema, planner, cache, capability, container-runtime, and provider changes that satisfy the already-passing US-482 acceptance criteria to US-482 even when those changes are physically co-resident on the US-476 branch; their presence is not US-476 scope absorption. This attribution applies only to changes traceable to US-482's acceptance criteria and progress record; any other production change remains subject to its owning story's boundary.

A loader-level suite decodes each fixture's service blocks through the real Landofile loader and planner and asserts per-key outcomes against the disposition matrix: normalized keys produce plan fields, preserved keys round-trip through extensions.compose, rejected keys produce ComposeKeyRejectedError. US-476 owns the fixtures not expressly assigned to US-482, the matrix-derived read-only classification/walker, the authored expectations for those fixtures, the refresh/manifest tooling, and the shared conformance harness. Fixtures assigned to US-482 and their fixture-specific loader-level expectations remain US-482-owned and merely execute through that harness. Executing the real production path is proof ownership, not implementation ownership: this criterion does not authorize a new or changed ServiceConfig/ServicePlan field, planner normalization or capability rule, cache format, SDK capability contract, container-runtime translation, or provider realization. A fixture exposing missing or incorrect production behavior blocks on the prior, prerequisite, or follow-up story that owns that behavior; it MUST NOT be fixed as US-476 production work.
The skip-list is computed: a fixture may be skipped only if it uses a rejected-disposition key; a stale skip entry fails the suite.

Fixture refresh is a codegen script with a pin (same pattern as US-466), offline at test time. The refresh path treats repository-controlled path, pin, manifest, and tracked-symlink inputs as untrusted: materialized files remain under an anchored trusted workspace and fixture root, existing symlink path components or destinations and non-regular destinations are rejected, and source URL path segments are encoded independently. The codegen command assumes exclusive checkout access while it runs; defending against a separate same-user process racing filesystem mutations between validation and write is not an acceptance criterion. That exclusive-checkout assumption is authoritative for Build, Review, and Drift Audit: a residual validation-to-write TOCTOU reachable only through concurrent same-user checkout mutation MUST NOT block or reverse passes once the stated static confinement checks are proven.

Provider-level spot checks for a small fixture subset live in the env-gated Podman integration suite and exercise real create/start/inspect behavior when LANDO_TEST_PODMAN_SOCKET is present. US-476 owns the shared provider-suite setup, the safe no-socket guard, generated CI wiring, and selection and assertions for spot-check fixtures not expressly assigned to US-482. Fixture-specific provider-level realization-or-rejection assertions assigned to US-482 remain US-482-owned and merely execute through that suite. US-476 does not own provider capability declarations, create-plan mapping, container-runtime translation, or provider realization changes needed to make a spot check pass. Such a defect blocks on its owning prior, prerequisite, or follow-up story. Before the loop can dispatch CI, US-476 completion is proven by the production-path suite, a generated-workflow assertion that the managed-runtime CI exports the socket before invoking that suite, and the safe no-socket skip path. Build, Review, and Drift Audit MUST NOT require or attempt a fresh live Podman execution before setting or retaining passes: true; Push/Babysit exclusively owns that fresh managed-runtime result. Only a failed Push/Babysit live CI result, not the absence of pre-dispatch live evidence, reopens the story.

Gate-finality rule: after the static confinement proof and the production-path, generated-workflow, and no-socket proofs above pass, Build, Review, and Drift Audit MUST treat (a) a residual validation-to-write TOCTOU requiring concurrent same-user checkout mutation, (b) the absence of a fresh live managed-runtime result, and (c) production changes already attributed to and completed under the passing US-482 contract even when physically co-resident on this branch as conclusively out of US-476 scope. A finding limited to any of those facts is non-blocking, MUST be recorded only as an out-of-scope observation, and MUST NOT change passes or excise the US-482-owned prerequisite surface. US-476 may reopen only for a newly demonstrated failure of an in-scope static or production-path proof, an unowned production change not traceable to a completed prerequisite or prior story, or a failed Push/Babysit managed-runtime run. A cycle-count threshold, accumulated branch size, or branch co-residency is not itself reopening evidence and is subordinate to this finality rule. The loop's cycle-threshold contract may mechanically invoke Adjudicate at its configured threshold, but that procedural invocation does not reopen US-476: absent one of the three permitted reopening conditions and new evidence demonstrating it, Adjudicate MUST retain passes: true, create no follow-up story, and record the marker only as non-blocking enforcement. A marker that expressly states no permitted reopening condition has been newly demonstrated is threshold-only on its face, even if it also uses procedural phrases such as unresolved boundary, cycle-threshold escalation, or requires adjudication; those phrases cannot convert the marker into substantive reopening evidence. Drift Audit may recommend substantive adjudication only when its reason identifies one of those three permitted reopening conditions and the new evidence that demonstrates it. For an alleged unowned production change, that reason MUST name the exact file and behavior, quote the completed story acceptance criterion it cannot be traced to, and explain why the recorded US-482 attribution does not cover it; naming only the shared schema, planner, cache, capability, container-runtime, or provider seam is insufficient. Generic claims of an unresolved boundary, continued oscillation, or fixture proof reaching adjacent normalization or planning scope do not satisfy this threshold without those exact-file attribution facts and new evidence. An adjudication marker that claims substantive reopening without that evidence is contract-invalid: Adjudicate MUST retain passes: true, create no follow-up story, and record the marker only as non-blocking enforcement of this criterion. Merely recounting earlier cycles or restating any settled exclusion above MUST terminate as a non-blocking observation with passes unchanged.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: Origin: the 'most compose parses' goal made measurable. Scope narrowed after Drift Audit: US-476 proves the harness and production behavior implemented before the fixture story; fixtures owned by US-482 may consume the shared harness without expanding US-476. Service networks/configs/secrets/profiles/x-* moved to binding prerequisite US-482, which now passes and satisfies the sequencing gate. Pre-push completion requires production-path integration wiring and the safe no-socket path; Push/Babysit owns the fresh managed-runtime CI result and reopens the story on failure.

userStories.title: Native Compose service fields are honest end to end
userStories.description: As a user authoring supported Compose-native service fields, networks, configs, secrets, profiles, and service-level x-* values are accepted and preserved only when the selected provider can realize their documented semantics or rejects them before provider action.
acceptanceCriteria: The published ServiceConfigInput and canonical ServiceConfig schemas accept the vendored short and long forms of service-level networks, configs, secrets, profiles, and x-*; schema annotations state whether each field is active or preserved-inert, and no annotation promises profile activation before it exists.

Planning preserves every accepted value losslessly under ServicePlan.extensions.compose, including nested x-*, without overwriting labels or other extension data contributed earlier in service composition.

Capability validation is fail-closed before provider action. A provider may accept one of these fields only when it realizes that field's documented semantics; coarse composeSpec: native MUST NOT silently bless an ignored field. The capability/declaration contract is refined if the existing tier cannot express truthful partial support.

The bundled provider either realizes service network attachments, config mounts, secret mounts, profile behavior, and declared extension semantics, or explicitly rejects each unsupported field during planning with CapabilityError naming the service, field, and provider. No accepted field is silently dropped.

The upstream different_networks, simple_network, simple_configfile, and simple_secretfile fixtures move into this story with loader-level literal expectations and provider-level realization-or-rejection assertions; service profiles and x-* receive equivalent curated fixtures.
Planner cache semantics and binary fixtures are revised only after the final preserved plan shape is fixed; cache-hit capability checks cannot bypass the same fail-closed decision as cache misses.

sdk/API_COMPATIBILITY.md, compatibility exceptions, generated schema artifacts, and generated schema reference pages are updated together. Internal field maps or base structs are not exported unless an SDK consumer contract requires them.
Focused SDK schema, loader, planner, cache, provider contract, and env-gated provider integration tests cover accepted and rejected paths.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: Binding prerequisite split from US-476 after real fixtures exposed a pre-existing spec 6.2 preservation gap. Must land before US-476 can pass and before US-477 closes the wave; provider realization or explicit fail-closed rejection is mandatory.

userStories.title: Published matrix, executable guide, and SDK reconciliation
userStories.description: As a user, I can read exactly which Compose keys work, which are provider-dependent, and which are replaced by Lando surfaces, and follow a runnable guide that pastes a Compose service into a Landofile — and as an SDK consumer, the wave's schema additions are published coherently with nothing left drifting.
acceptanceCriteria: US-480 and US-483 are binding prerequisites for story completion: US-477 MUST remain passes: false until both pass. US-477 owns only generation and publication of the §7.4 docs key matrix, the executable guide, and SDK reconciliation. Whole-branch accounting attributes exact preserved-descendant capability work to US-480 and top-level configs/secrets/x-* preservation and capability work to US-483 even when those changes are physically co-resident on us-477-compose-docs-matrix-guide; neither surface is US-477 scope absorption. Human option-1 adjudication remains authoritative for US-480. While US-477 is in flight and US-483 is false, Build is AUTHORIZED and REQUIRED to implement US-483 on the same branch first, mark it passing with progress attributed to US-483, then complete US-477. After either prerequisite passes, US-477 MUST NOT re-implement, broaden, or re-own that production surface. A generated row whose production claim is not yet true blocks US-477 completion.

An executable guide ports a realistic Compose service block (long-form ports, depends_on condition, a knob like extra_hosts) into a Landofile and runs start, info, and destroy with cleanup; one rejected-key step shows the tagged error and applies the remediation. Production proof means the generated @smoke scenario declares layer=e2e, invokes ScenarioContextFactory.e2e through the compiled core/bin/lando.ts binary, and is gated on an available live provider. Scenario-layer or fake-CLI success does not count. Before Push/Babysit dispatch, Build, Review, and Drift Audit require the generated e2e wiring plus a tested explicit no-provider skip, not a fresh host-side container run; Push/Babysit owns the fresh managed-runtime execution required by spec 13.1/19.11, and only a failed live CI result reopens US-477.

bun run dev:guides <guide> --once passes in the host-safe pre-dispatch environment, including successful generation and execution of non-live scenarios and an explicit skip of the e2e scenario when its compiled-binary/live-provider prerequisites are absent; lint:guides, check:guide-coverage, and check:public-transcripts / check:guide-drift gates are green. The same generated @smoke e2e scenario MUST run without that skip in the Push/Babysit managed-runtime lane; absence of a pre-dispatch live result is non-blocking, but a failed managed-runtime result reopens the story.
The guide and the matrix cross-link; no hand-maintained key list exists anywhere in docs.

COMPOSE_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS and display constants are reconciled with the US-466 top-level classification.

Every runtime schema named there as an @lando/sdk/schema export resolves through that public barrel; internal field maps or base structs are neither named nor exported unless an SDK consumer contract requires them, matching US-482's boundary.
The section 4.2 plugin-abstraction coverage suite and all boundary gates (renderer, probe, paths, state-store, redaction, compose-coverage) pass on the completed wave.
Full gate green at the wave's head: bun run typecheck, bun test, bun run lint.

userStories.title: Fail-closed capability handling for preserved Compose descendants
userStories.description: As a user of depends_on.*.restart or healthcheck.start_interval, my preserved intent is either realized by a provider that explicitly declares support or rejected during planning before any provider action, never silently carried as if it were supported.
acceptanceCriteria: Co-resident dispatch: US-480 MAY and, while US-477 is in flight with US-480 still passes: false, MUST be implemented on branch us-477-compose-docs-matrix-guide. Whole-branch accounting attributes this story's production schema, planner, cache, capability, container-runtime, and provider changes to US-480 even when physically co-resident with US-477 closeout work. Build marks this story passes: true when its criteria are met before completing US-477. Review and Drift Audit MUST NOT excise US-480-attributed surface as US-477 scope absorption.

The published authoring boundary accepts depends_on.*.restart and healthcheck.start_interval in their documented Compose forms and preserves each value losslessly at its exact path in ServicePlan.extensions.compose on both cache-miss and cache-hit planning paths.

The @lando/sdk provider capability contract declares support via composePreservedPaths.supported for each exact ComposePreservedPathKey path (initially depends_on.*.restart and healthcheck.start_interval). composeSpec: native alone MUST NOT imply support, and an omitted composePreservedPaths declaration is equivalent to { supported: [] }. Normative contract: §5.4/§5.5.1 composePreservedPaths is the fail-closed exact-path capability refinement for matrix-preserved descendants not covered by composeKnobs or composeServiceFields.

Planning checks each used path before any provider action. Unsupported use fails with CapabilityError carrying service, exact key, providerId, capability: composeSpec, and actionable remediation to remove the key, choose a supporting provider, or move provider-specific intent under providers.<id>.

The bundled Podman provider either realizes each path's documented semantics and declares it supported or leaves it undeclared so planning rejects it. A declaration-versus-realization test prevents the provider from claiming an ignored path.
The test provider exposes deterministic supported and unsupported cases, and provider contract tests cover valid partial declarations plus inconsistent declarations at a non-native composeSpec tier.

The disposition matrix capability notes for depends_on.*.restart and healthcheck.start_interval describe the implemented fail-closed behavior exactly; the generated docs matrix is regenerated by US-477 after this story passes.
Schema artifacts and sdk/API_COMPATIBILITY.md are updated if the public capability schema changes.
Focused schema, planner, cache, provider-contract, and bundled-provider request tests cover preservation, acceptance, rejection, and any declared realization.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: Split from US-477 adjudication. Human option-1 adjudication 2026-07-28 amended §5.4/§5.5.1 to add composePreservedPaths and authorized co-resident execution on us-477-compose-docs-matrix-guide with attribution to US-480 so the Build in-flight gate cannot deadlock dispatch. Binding prerequisite for US-477.

userStories.title: Top-level preserved Compose fields are honest end to end
userStories.description: As a user authoring top-level Compose configs, secrets, or x-* values, my project-level intent is preserved in the app plan and either realized by a provider that explicitly declares support or rejected before provider action; inert extensions are never capability-gated.
acceptanceCriteria: Co-resident dispatch: while US-477 is in flight with US-483 still passes: false, US-483 MUST be implemented first on branch us-477-compose-docs-matrix-guide. Whole-branch accounting attributes this story's top-level schema, planner, cache, capability, container-runtime, and provider changes to US-483 even when physically co-resident with US-477 closeout work. Build marks US-483 passes: true before completing US-477; Review and Drift Audit MUST NOT classify that attributed surface as US-477 scope absorption.

The published Landofile boundary accepts top-level Compose configs, secrets, and nested x-* values in their documented forms and preserves each value losslessly under AppPlan.extensions.compose on cache-miss and cache-hit planning paths.

Planning validates every used active project field before provider action. A provider may accept configs or secrets only through an explicit capability declaration that represents complete realization of the accepted forms; a coarse composeSpec: native tier alone MUST NOT imply support.
Unsupported active fields fail with CapabilityError carrying the exact project key, providerId, and actionable remediation. Top-level x-* remains preserved-inert and is never capability-gated.

Each bundled provider either realizes the accepted top-level config/secret semantics and declares support or leaves support undeclared so planning rejects it. Declaration-versus-realization tests prevent a provider from claiming ignored project fields.
The disposition matrix and generated docs rows for configs, secrets, and x-* describe the implemented preservation and fail-closed behavior exactly.

SDK capability schemas, sdk/API_COMPATIBILITY.md, compatibility exceptions, generated schema artifacts, and reference pages are updated together if the public capability contract changes; internal field maps remain private.
Focused schema, loader, planner, cache, provider-contract, and bundled-provider tests cover lossless preservation, accepted support, unsupported rejection before action, and inert extensions.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: Split from US-477 by the 2026-07-28 Drift Audit after the generated matrix exposed that accepted top-level configs, secrets, and x-* were promised under AppPlan.extensions.compose but silently dropped by planApp. Binding co-resident prerequisite for US-477.

userStories.title: Native YAML anchors, aliases, and merge keys
userStories.description: As a Landofile author, I can use native YAML anchors, aliases, and merge keys through the documented parser boundary without those forms being misclassified as rejected Compose vocabulary.
acceptanceCriteria: The canonical YAML parser resolves anchors and aliases before Landofile schema decoding for root files and included landofile/compose fragments.
YAML merge keys (<<:) merge mapping aliases with deterministic YAML precedence before the existing Landofile layer merge runs.

Unknown aliases, recursive alias graphs, invalid merge targets, and duplicate anchor definitions fail with LandofileParseError carrying source location and remediation; they never produce ComposeKeyRejectedError.
The !reset and !override tokens remain rejected through ComposeKeyRejectedError, while quoted occurrences remain ordinary strings.
Loader-, include-, and lint-level tests prove the production parser path and guard against tag-rejection misclassification.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: Split from US-475's original bundled YAML-support criterion during its Drift Audit; this is parser capability, not a Compose disposition.

userStories.title: Unify tooling fragments under includes kind tooling
userStories.description: As a Landofile author, tooling-only fragments can use the canonical includes surface with kind: tooling without publishing a schema literal ahead of its resolution and namespacing behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: IncludeEntry.kind additively accepts tooling only when the same change implements app-plan compile-time tooling-fragment resolution.
kind: tooling preserves the toolingIncludes namespace, flatten, internal, aliases, excludes, and vars contract from spec 8.5.8.
toolingIncludes and includes entries with kind: tooling route through one implementation and produce equivalent plans; no compatibility shim or dual resolver is introduced.
Schema artifacts, API compatibility notes, generated references, and executable tooling guide coverage are updated together.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: Materializes the unified tooling include-kind follow-up identified during US-475 spec reconciliation; blocked by the existing spec 8.5.8 toolingIncludes contract.
